tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in a biology class.

questions.stem: How does the speaker define the term "keystone species"?

options.A: Any species that provides food or habitat for other populations
options.B: Any species that has been permanently removed from its environment
options.C: Any species that plays an outsized role in the functioning of its ecosystem
options.D: Any species that conservationists protect to maintain ecological balance

questions.stem: How do sea otters help maintain the health of an ecosystem?

options.A: By containing the growth of kelp forests
options.B: By controlling the population of sea urchins
options.C: By promoting a diverse population of herbivores
options.D: By producing new habitats for other marine species

questions.stem: What function do African elephants perform as a savanna keystone species?

options.B: They suppress the growth of grasses.
options.D: They maintain the health of forest ecosystems.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker talk about wolves?

options.A: To provide an example of a keystone species that has become extinct
options.B: To illustrate the impact on an ecosystem of a missing keystone species
options.C: To suggest that keystone species can be replaced by a different species
options.D: To explain why a keystone species might suddenly disappear from an ecosystem

tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in a sociology class.

questions.stem: What is the main topic of the talk?

options.A: The impact of governmental policies on educational equality
options.B: Recent efforts to remove barriers to social mobility
options.C: Factors related to individuals' ability to advance in a society
options.D: The impact of social inequality on education

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about education?

options.A: It has been determined to be the leading indicator of one's socioeconomic status.
options.B: It is often the key to advancing upward in the social hierarchy.
options.C: It is not always needed to obtain a high-paying job.
options.D: It rarely leads to upward social mobility.

questions.stem: What does the speaker suggest about regions with thriving economies?

options.A: They provide more jobs in the manufacturing sector than other regions do.
options.B: They are less concerned about social mobility than other regions are.
options.C: They offer more opportunities for social advancement than other regions do.
options.D: They receive more governmental assistance than other regions do.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker talk about policymakers?

options.A: To provide an example of a profession that impacts social mobility
options.B: To highlight the need for higher levels of education in a society
options.C: To point out that some groups advance through society more quickly than others
options.D: To propose a solution for achieving social equality
